faq.q: I'm from the US / UK / Japan / EU. Do I need K-ETA?
faq.a: Not right now — those are on the 22-country waiver through 31 Dec 2026, so you skip K-ETA and just file the free e-Arrival Card. This is scheduled to change on 1 Jan 2027.

faq.q: Is K-ETA the same as a visa?
faq.a: No. K-ETA is a travel authorization that lets you board and enter visa-free; it is not a visa. If your nationality isn't visa-free, you still need an actual visa from a Korean embassy.

faq.q: How long is K-ETA valid?
faq.a: Three years from approval, with multiple entries — so one approval usually covers repeat trips until it expires or your passport does.

faq.q: How much does it cost and is it refundable?
faq.a: ₩10,000 (about US$8). The fee is non-refundable, even if your application is declined.

faq.q: How early should I apply?
faq.a: At least 72 hours before boarding. Many approvals come within minutes, but leave a buffer in case yours is reviewed.

faq.q: Do children and seniors need K-ETA?
faq.a: Historically travelers 17 and under or 65 and over have been exempt from K-ETA. Confirm the current age rule at k-eta.go.kr before you rely on it.

faq.q: What's the e-Arrival Card and do I really need it?
faq.a: It's the digital version of the paper arrival card, filed free at e-arrivalcard.go.kr up to 72 hours before you land. Most short-term visitors need it; valid K-ETA holders and registered residents are exempt.

faq.q: Which sites are official?
faq.a: Only k-eta.go.kr (K-ETA) and e-arrivalcard.go.kr (arrival card). Anything charging a big 'service fee' is a third-party reseller, not the government.

faq.q: Can I get a visa on arrival at the airport?
faq.a: No — Korea doesn't offer a general visa on arrival for tourists. Visa-free nationals enter with no visa (plus K-ETA if required and the e-Arrival Card); everyone else must obtain a visa in advance at a Korean embassy or Visa Application Center.

faq.q: How do I apply for K-ETA, step by step?
faq.a: Apply only at the official site k-eta.go.kr (or the K-ETA app), at least 72 hours before boarding. Upload a passport photo, answer the travel questions and pay ₩10,000. Approval is often fast but can take up to 72 hours, and a K-ETA is valid 3 years with multiple entries.

faq.q: My K-ETA was refused — what can I do?
faq.a: A refusal doesn't automatically ban you, but you can't board on it. Recheck your answers and reapply carefully, or apply for the appropriate visa at a Korean embassy. Immigration still makes the final decision on arrival, and you should only ever use k-eta.go.kr.

faq.q: Do I need a K-ETA or visa just to transit through Korea?
faq.a: If you stay airside and don't clear immigration, you generally need neither. If you leave the airport — including some transit-tour programs — you are entering Korea and the normal rules apply. Confirm with your airline and the official sites for your route.

faq.q: How long can I stay without a visa?
faq.a: It depends on your nationality — commonly up to 90 days for tourism, though some nationalities get 30 days and a few have their own limits. Check your country's guide above, and never overstay.

faq.q: What happens if I overstay, and can I extend my stay?
faq.a: Overstaying brings fines and possible bans on future entry. Short-term visa-free and tourist stays usually can't be extended; for longer you must apply for the right visa. Immigration matters are handled through HiKorea (hikorea.go.kr).

faq.q: When does the K-ETA waiver end and K-ETA come back?
faq.a: The temporary waiver for the 22 exempt countries and regions runs through 31 December 2026, and K-ETA is scheduled to return on 1 January 2027 unless it is extended again. Reconfirm at k-eta.go.kr close to your travel date.

faq.q: Do I need both K-ETA and the e-Arrival Card?
faq.a: No — you file one or the other. A valid K-ETA exempts you from the e-Arrival Card. If K-ETA is waived for your nationality (or you're exempt by age — 17 and under or 65 and over), file the free e-Arrival Card at e-arrivalcard.go.kr instead.

faq.q: Do Bangladeshi citizens need a visa for Korea?

faq.q: What is the e-Form?
faq.a: Since 2026 every applicant must complete the online e-Form on visa.go.kr and print it — the printout has a barcode that the embassy scans. Handwritten old forms are not accepted.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually about 10–15 working days, and longer during peak season or if you're called for an interview or extra documents. Apply well ahead of your trip.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: About US$40 for a single-entry short-term visa; roughly US$70 for double entry and US$90 for multiple entry. Amounts change — confirm the current fee at the embassy.

faq.q: What is a Bank Solvency Certificate?
faq.a: A letter from your bank confirming you are financially solvent. Bangladesh applicants are usually expected to submit it in addition to the 6-month bank statement.

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faq.a: Double- and multiple-entry visas are available for a higher fee, but eligibility varies. Ask at the embassy about current rules for Bangladesh.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
faq.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.

faq.q: Can tour groups still enter visa-free?

faq.q: Where do I apply?

faq.q: How much money do I need to show?

faq.a: A minimum of about 15 working days, and longer for some cases. There is no express service, so apply well ahead of your trip.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: The fee is paid in Sri Lankan rupees at the rate in the embassy's current 'Visa Fee Increase' notice. Confirm the exact amount on the embassy site.

faq.q: Is there an express or urgent option?
faq.a: No. Early issuance is only available for diplomatic and official passport holders.

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faq.a: Multiple-entry tourist visas are possible in some cases, but eligibility varies. Ask at the embassy about current rules for Sri Lanka.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
faq.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.

faq.q: Taiwan → Korea: do you need a visa?
faq.a: No tourist visa needed — Taiwan passports are visa-free. For short-term tourism you don't apply for any visa. Right now K-ETA is waived too, so the main thing to do is file the free e-Arrival Card before you land.

faq.q: Do travelers from Taiwan need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: No — for short-term tourism Taiwan passport holders enter Korea visa-free. You do not apply for any tourist visa.

faq.q: Do I need K-ETA?
faq.a: Not right now. Taiwan is among the 22 countries exempt from K-ETA through 31 Dec 2026. The requirement is scheduled to return on 1 Jan 2027 unless extended.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
faq.a: Yes — most visitors file the free e-Arrival Card at e-arrivalcard.go.kr, within 72 hours before arrival.

faq.q: How long can I stay?
faq.a: Up to 90 days, for tourism.

faq.q: Can I work or study on this entry?
faq.a: No. Visa-free entry is for tourism and short visits only; working or studying requires the appropriate visa.

faq.q: When does K-ETA come back?
faq.a: The waiver is scheduled to end on 31 Dec 2026, with K-ETA resuming 1 Jan 2027 unless extended — reconfirm close to your travel date.

faq.q: Thailand → Korea: do you need a visa?
faq.a: No tourist visa needed — but you must apply for K-ETA. Thai passports are visa-free for short tourism, so there's no visa to apply for. But Thailand is not on the K-ETA waiver list, so you must get a K-ETA before you fly. With a valid K-ETA you're then exempt from the e-Arrival Card.

faq.q: Do Thai passport holders need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: No — for short-term tourism, Thai passport holders enter Korea visa-free and can stay up to 90 days. You do not apply for any tourist visa.

faq.q: Do I need K-ETA?
faq.a: Yes. Thailand is not on the temporary K-ETA waiver list, so you must apply for K-ETA before boarding — at the official site k-eta.go.kr.

faq.q: How much is K-ETA and how long is it valid?
faq.a: It costs KRW 10,000 (about US$8), is valid for 3 years, and allows multiple entries. Apply only at k-eta.go.kr.

faq.q: Is K-ETA approval guaranteed?
faq.a: No. A K-ETA, and the final decision by immigration on arrival, are not guaranteed. Apply early, answer honestly, and carry genuine tourism documents — return ticket, hotel booking and proof of funds.

faq.q: Do I also need the e-Arrival Card?
faq.a: No — if you hold a valid K-ETA you're exempt from the e-Arrival Card. You file one or the other, not both.

faq.q: How long can I stay?
faq.a: Up to 90 days, for tourism. Working or studying requires the appropriate visa.

faq.q: Uzbekistan → Korea: do you need a visa?
faq.a: Yes — Uzbekistani passport holders need a visa. You'll apply for the C-3 short-term tourist visa (stay up to 90 days). For tourism the Korean Embassy in Tashkent accepts documents ONLY through accredited travel agencies — you can't submit directly or online. K-ETA/visa-free entry does NOT apply.

faq.q: Do Uzbekistani citizens need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: Yes — for tourism you apply in advance for the C-3 short-term tourist visa. Uzbekistani passports are not visa-free and not on the K-ETA list.

faq.q: Can I apply directly at the embassy or online?
faq.a: Not for a tourist visa. The Korean Embassy in Tashkent accepts tourist applications only through travel agencies it has accredited. Employment, some student and government-program visas are submitted differently.

faq.q: Where do I find the accredited agencies?
faq.a: The official list is published on the Korean Embassy in Tashkent's website. Use only agencies on that list.

faq.q: How much does it cost and how long does it take?
faq.a: The fee and processing time aren't published in an accessible official source. Confirm both with an accredited agency or the embassy before you book flights.

faq.q: Where is the embassy?
faq.a: The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Tashkent is at Afrosiyob Street 7, Mirabad District — but for tourism you submit through an accredited agency, not in person.

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?

faq.q: Vietnam → Korea: do you need a visa?
faq.a: Yes — Vietnamese passport holders need a visa. You'll apply for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa in person at a Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC) in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City. The good news: the paperwork was simplified and long-validity visas are expanding.

faq.q: Do Vietnamese citizens need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: Yes, for mainland Korea you apply in advance for the C-3-9 tourist visa. (Ordinary passports are not visa-free for Korea.)

faq.q: Can I get a 5- or 10-year visa?
faq.a: Korea has been expanding multi-year, multiple-entry visas for Vietnamese travelers. Eligibility depends on your profile and travel history — ask the KVAC/embassy whether you qualify.

faq.q: Where do I apply?
faq.a: At the Korea Visa Application Center in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, depending on where you live, or the Korean embassy/consulate.

faq.q: How much money do I need to prove?
faq.a: There's no fixed minimum. Show a stable balance and strong ties to Vietnam. Financial proof is now simplified to 1–2 types.

faq.q: How much is the fee?
faq.a: Fees are set by reciprocity and vary; they are non-refundable even if refused. Confirm the current amount at your KVAC.

faq.q: I'm going on a company incentive trip — simpler?
faq.a: Yes. For company-organized group tours, the organizing company's guarantee can replace individual financial documents.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
faq.a: Entry-document rules like the e-Arrival Card can still apply on arrival. Check the current rules close to your travel date.
